claims.claim: The three common plate-boundary types are divergent, convergent, and transform.

At divergent boundaries plates move apart and new crust is generated; at convergent boundaries one plate can descend beneath another and crust is recycled; at transform boundaries plates slide horizontally past one another without creating or destroying lithosphere.

Divergent boundaries commonly have shallow earthquakes and volcanism, convergent settings can have earthquakes at a variety of depths and volcanic arcs, and transform settings commonly have shallow earthquakes with little or no volcanism.
Some plate boundaries are broad zones rather than simple lines, so a map classification can be uncertain or more complex than the three introductory types.
Boundary type is inferred from relative motion and multiple geological and geophysical observations, not from one landform alone.
